Chevy’s Corvette E-Ray Convertible 3LZ Is Now a Five-Digit Affair in USA
13 photos
Photo: Cars&Bids
Chevrolet may have pulled the plug on the E-Ray version of the C8-generation Corvette, replacing it with the Grand Sport X , but that does not make the first-ever electrified variant of the ‘Vette, as well as the first one to feature all-wheel drive, any less exciting.
In fact, these things are still worth a lot of money on the used car market, but if you know where to look and are patient enough, then you could land one for five digits. Mind you, it does not have to be a beaten-up example that has seen plenty of action over the years, because you could aim straight for an open-top 3LZ that is still brand new, and has had a single owner in the papers ever since it left the dealership.
Don’t believe us? Well, then you should know that the ‘Vette pictured in the gallery changed hands for $99,500. It is a 2025 model year Chevrolet Corvette E-Ray Convertible 3LZ , which was bought by the seller new back in March 2025. The man paid $136,890, as per the attached window sticker, and after putting only 570 miles (920 km) on the clock, he decided to let it go, stating that him and the missus are driving something bigger, and he does not have the time to enjoy the blue-collar electrified supercar.
Do you somehow think that this machine must have been involved in an accident, or that the mileage is not real? That’s not the case, because the Carfax history report reveals that the Arctic White paint finish has never touched or has been touched by another vehicle, nor something solid for that matter, and that the mileage is correct. This ride has a clean Iowa title, and before being sold, it was located in Clive, IA.
Photo: Cars&Bids There is no flaws category in the listing that we will link toward the end of the story, and if you must know, there are no modifications either. This 2025 Chevy Corvette E-Ray Convertible 3LZ features 20-inch wheels at the front and 21-inch wheels at the rear, which are backed up by the carbon ceramic brakes, and also benefits from the Magnetic Selective Ride Control, and the nose-lift system with memory function.
Other notable equipment mentioned in the ad includes the power-retractable hardtop, Adrenaline Red stitching, Torch Red seatbelts, and carbon fiber and sueded steering wheel. Suede is the material that dominates the cockpit, and there are several red inserts for contrast, as mentioned above, which also include the red 12 o’clock marker on the steering wheel. And the wall of buttons is also present, if you are into that sort of thing.
Care to talk about the firepower? Well, as you likely know, the Chevrolet Corvette E-Ray came with a 6.2-liter V8, shared with the era’s Stingray (the latest model year has a 6.7L V8), and with the electric trickery up and running, it had 655 hp (489 kW/664 ps) and 595 pound-feet (807 Nm) of torque in total. The model took just 2.5 seconds to reach 60 mph (97 kph), and that’s almost as fast as the Lamborghini Revuelto, which costs a lot more.
Due to the low mileage, the pictured Chevy Corvette E-Ray has not required any servicing yet, the seller noted. Besides the car, the new owner will also get the window sticker, as well as the usual manuals, two key fobs, a trickle charger, and a serialized crystal glass model.
Photo: Cars&Bids Nationwide listings for the Chevrolet Corvette E-Ray usually span from over $85,000 to more than $120,000 in today’s used car market, and the value depends on the trim level (1LZ, 2LZ, or 3LZ), as well as the body style, mileage, and overall appearance. Brand new examples with a single owner in the papers since new do not tend to fall into the five-digit category, but as we already told you above, this one did.
So, congratulations to the new owner for landing a great machine that was almost $137,000 new some one and a half years ago. This ride depreciated $37,390, and it ended up costing the seller a whopping $65+ per mile. A chauffeured limo service would have been more than ten times more affordable. It is worth noting that the title will become available only after the loan has been paid off, and the sale proceeds will be used to satisfy it.
This particular 2025 Chevrolet Corvette E-Ray Convertible 3LZ changed hands recently as part of an online auction that ended on November 12, 2026. It was advertised on Cars&Bids, and if you want to find out more about it, and check it out in additional pictures, then you should access the listing here . However, before you do that, let us know if you would have paid $99,500 for it, given that it is a brand new example with zero issues.
